 Warriors vs. Lakers injury report: Brandin Podziemski out, Steph Curry probable
 The full injury report for Wednesday’s game between Golden State and Los Angeles.
 by Brady Klopfer Oct 22, 2026, 12:21 AM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 It’s finally time! After a long and arduous offseason, the 2026-27 NBA season has arrived, and with it the first game of the season for the Golden State Warriors, who visit the Los Angeles Lakers to kick off the year.
 The Dubs, unfortunately, are far from at full strength for the first game of the year, while the Lakers are fairly healthy. Here’s the complete injury report for both teams.
 Warriors
 Out — Brandin Podziemski (bilateral low back soreness) 
 Podziemski figures to have a huge role in his fourth NBA season. He shined in the preseason, and recently inked a five-year, $110 million deal. So it’s a bummer that he’ll miss the opener , but after suffering from some back soreness late in camp, he won’t be able to suit up. Thankfully he isn’t expected to be out long.
 Out — Charles Bassey (right patellar tendinopathy) 
 Bassey might have been in line to start tonight, as he did in the preseason finale, if he were healthy. Unfortunately, he suffered a mild injury in that finale, and that will cost him the opener . As with Podziemski, it’s not considered a serious injury, and he should be back on the court soon.
 Out — Kristaps Porziņģis (not with team) 
 The latest news about Porziņģis isn’t good. He’s not with the team, the Warriors are already looking at trading his contract, and the Latvian All-Star is reportedly considering calling it a career. It’s fair to wonder if he’ll ever play for the Warriors again, and with both he and Bassey out, you can expect two-way center Graham Ike to get a lot of playing time.
 Out — Jimmy Butler III (right ACL repair surgery) 
 No surprises here. Butler remains sidelined indefinitely, and is likely targeting a second-half return.
 Out — Moses Moody (right patellar tendon repair surgery) 
 And no surprises here, either. Moody is likely a few months from returning from the knee injury that ended his 2025-26 season. There’s no set timetable yet.
 Probable — Steph Curry (right ankle soreness) 
 When Curry limped off the court at open practice on Sunday, it seemed like he might be out for a while. Instead, he thankfully is expected to play in the opener.
 Lakers
 Out — Collin Sexton (right soleus strain) 
 Sexton figures to play a huge role in his first year with the purple and gold, but his debut will have to wait. He shouldn’t be sidelined long, but won’t play in the opener.
 Out — Cameron Carr (right oblique strain) 
 Carr was a late first-round pick, following a breakout campaign at Baylor a year ago. He likely won’t have to wait long to make his NBA debut, but it won’t be tonight.
 Out — Adou Thiero (left knee effusion swelling) 
 Thiero had a modest role last year with the Lakers, appearing in 25 games and averaging 6.0 minutes per game in his rookie season. He’ll look to build on that this year, but will have to wait as it won’t happen tonight.
 Available — Walker Kessler (left finger splint) 
 LA’s big offseason acquisition was a question mark in the days leading up to the opener, but has now been cleared to play. The Warriors have a serious disadvantage in the paint between Kessler’s availability and their own lack of centers.
 Enjoy the game, everyone! It tips off at 7:00 p.m. PT on ESPN.
